text: Is that... that's my flour! My stamp on the sack and everything. The smugglers had it? Course they did. Took six bags off my cart on the cove road a fortnight back.
You came all the way round the island with it. Nobody comes round this side. Here, for your trouble, and take a loaf or two off Ida on me.
The rest? Eaten, I expect. Smugglers bake terrible bread. You can tell by looking at them.
Go on, Vey'll want to hear it went well. And come back at harvest. The fields are a sight.
Mind the sails when they're turning. I've lost two hats that way.
Brann. I keep the mill and the mill keeps me. Most of the bread in Brinehollow started on my stones.

menu.text: What can I do for you?

text: Wheat, greens, the vines and the orchard by the south road. Joss and Wynn work the rows. I grind what they grow.
Flour goes to Ida, bread goes to Gus, and Gus soaks it in stew. Somebody has to start it.
The highland, and the falls off it into a pool you can swim in. Down the road past the farmhouses there's a cove with old Gannet's hut.
East along the coast there's a wreck on the rocks. Gannet says she's still got her crew. Gannet says a lot of things.
